hens_rule_text: Up to 6 chicken hens allowed by right in single-family residential zones (R-1, R-1A, R-2) with no permit; more than 6 needs a multipet permit.
permit_notes: No permit for 6 or fewer hens in qualifying residential zones. Keeping more than 6 requires a multipet permit from the Director of Animal Services.
setback_notes: Enclosure must be in the rear yard; an enclosure under 200 sq ft needs at least a 5 ft setback from a side or rear property line, not a distance from neighboring homes. Enclosures over 200 sq ft follow the zoning code's general setback rules (Chapter 40).
coop_rules: Hens must stay confined to a rear-yard enclosure; litter and droppings collected daily into a closed, rat-proof, fly-tight container.
zoning_notes: Applies in R-1, R-1A and R-2 residential districts; other zoning may differ.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 4 (Animals), Article 4.01 and Division on Livestock and Other Animals

sources.name: City of Lubbock, TX Code of Ordinances, Livestock and Other Animals (eCode360)
KFYO, Lubbock's Rules For Keeping Backyard Chickens At Home

research_notes: Facts come from search-result extracts of the city's eCode360-hosted code (setback and rear-yard rules) and a local news summary of the hen cap and multipet permit rule; the full eCode360 page could not be opened directly from this machine (Cloudflare block). Texas has no state cap on city rules and HOAs can still restrict chickens; no 2023 to 2026 amendment was found.
